bugs: Mention regex `(?<![\w@])@(\w+)` (app/Models/Reply.php:33) stops at '.' or '-'. A body with '@john.doe' notifies an existing user 'john' instead of 'john.doe'. The factory avoids this by generating only [a-z0-9_] usernames, but nothing in the app enforces that format.
Regex has no /u flag, so non-ASCII usernames (e.g. 'åse') can never be mentioned, even though the model lowercases with mb_strtolower (probe confirmed).
antipatterns: app/Mail/MentionedInReply.php:21-22 builds HTML by string concatenation through Content(htmlString:) instead of a Blade or markdown view
app/Models/Reply.php:31 puts a mention-parsing query on the model; a small scope or query method on User would sit more naturally
Thread has no in-memory reply_count default, so a freshly created model reports null until refreshed (minor)
strengths: Thin invokable controller, a CreateReply action, and a FormRequest that uses validated('body')
Transaction wraps the insert and increment; mail and notifications go out only after commit
Builds the reply with replies()->make() and user()->associate() and keeps fillable limited to body
Factory username format matches what the mention parser accepts
Strongest test suite: exact-message validation, data payload check, mailable render with escaping, plain and JSON 401, a failure path that asserts nothing sent and the counter unchanged

database/factories/UserFactory.php:29 generates a username format the app's own parser cannot match

v.rationale: All three pass their own suites (12 tests each). All use a transaction for the insert and the increment and send mail and notifications only after it commits. impl-1 and impl-2 are almost line-for-line the same: a thin controller, an action class, and mentionedUsers() on Reply with the regex @(\w+). The difference is the factory. impl-2 uses faker userName(), which often produces dotted names. Its own parser can't match those: the probe showed 15 of 30 factory users could not be mentioned, and '@john.doe' notified a different user, 'john'. Sending to the wrong person is a real bug. impl-1 generates usernames that only use characters its parser accepts, so it is internally consistent. It also has the strongest tests (mailable rendering and escaping, notification payload, exact validation messages). Its weakness is an HTML string built inline in the mailable. impl-3 is less polished: a heavier controller, user_id, thread_id and reply_count mass-assignable, array_* helpers instead of collections, and unused Queueable traits. But its mention regex handles dots, hyphens and trailing punctuation. It was the only one to pass the dotted-name and factory-mentionability probes, and its tests also cover the unique-username constraint. Every implementation fails on non-ASCII usernames. A failure in the increment step rolled back cleanly with nothing sent in all three. Weighting correctness heavily: impl-3 > impl-1 > impl-2.
